name: control-no-op
why: Proves the battery's own plumbing reports green when nothing is broken.
asserts: A custom dashboard view is posted exactly as typed

name: protocol-relative-host-is-admitted
why: `//evil.example/x` is a host, not a path; the browser would leave the instance.
asserts: nothingThatLeavesThisHomeAssistantIsEverCanonical

name: traversal-suffix-is-safe
why: Chromium canonicalizes %2e%2e before navigating, so an unchecked suffix escapes the dashboard.
replace:
private fun safeSuffixSegment(segment: String): Boolean {
        if (true) return true
asserts: aTraversalBelowALegalRootIsRefusedAsARouteButStillNamesThatRoot

name: bare-root-is-not-auto
why: If `/` stopped meaning Auto the validator would reject the historic spelling of follow-the-default.
asserts: onlyRoutesThatNameNoDashboardFollowTheAccountDefault

name: validator-accepts-anything
why: The whole point of the spec validator: a path the renderer would discard must not persist.
asserts: a path that could never address a dashboard here is refused at the API

name: validator-blocks-unknown-dashboards
why: Existence is a runtime fact; blocking it would stop a panel being configured before its dashboard exists.
asserts: an unknown but well-formed dashboard is saveable because existence is a runtime fact

name: value-is-stored-uncanonicalised
why: Two spellings of one dashboard defeat the picker's list comparison and the no-op save detection.
asserts: a view below a dashboard root is accepted and stored canonically

name: empty-custom-path-is-not-required
why: An empty box would post blank, which the server accepts as Auto — the silent failure this feature removes.
asserts: An empty custom dashboard path never reaches the server as Auto

name: validity-scan-stops-at-the-first-control
why: The select precedes the input and is always valid, so the row would report clean and post the blank.
asserts: An empty custom dashboard path never reaches the server as Auto

name: sentinel-is-posted-as-a-path
why: The literal __custom__ would be saved and then rejected by the API, hiding a UI bug behind a server error.
asserts: Returning to Custom without retyping still posts the retained path

name: abandoned-custom-path-survives-switching-to-auto
why: Choosing Auto must post a blank, not the path the user just abandoned.
asserts: Switching Custom to Auto and to a listed dashboard posts each choice

name: custom-input-never-hides
why: A stale visible path input beside a chosen catalogue dashboard is an unreadable control.
asserts: Switching Custom to Auto and to a listed dashboard posts each choice

name: hidden-attribute-loses-to-the-display-rule
why: .hd-custom sets display, which beats the hidden attribute's UA style unless this rule exists.
asserts: Switching Custom to Auto and to a listed dashboard posts each choice

name: unknown-dashboard-root-is-never-flagged
why: Without the warning the renderer silently shows a different dashboard and nothing explains why.
asserts: A view under an unknown dashboard warns but is still saveable

name: every-custom-path-is-flagged-unknown
why: Warning on a perfectly good path trains the user to ignore the warning.
asserts: A view under an unknown dashboard warns but is still saveable

name: picker-overflows-a-narrow-panel
why: The wrapper must track its column, not a fixed width, or the native popup escapes the card.
asserts: The dashboard picker fits a 480px panel without overflowing its card

name: surfaces-disagree-about-the-sentinel
why: Divergent sentinels mean a value one surface treats as Custom the other saves as a literal path.
asserts: bothSurfacesAgreeOnWhatACustomDashboardPathLooksLike

name: surfaces-disagree-about-what-a-path-looks-like
why: One surface would accept shapes the other rejects, so the same typing succeeds or fails by page.
asserts: bothSurfacesAgreeOnWhatACustomDashboardPathLooksLike

name: wizard-submits-an-incomplete-custom-path
why: The wizard has no native form validity, so its own gate is the only thing stopping a blank answer.
asserts: anEmptyCustomPathCannotBeSavedAsASilentAuto

name: wizard-select-writes-the-sentinel-first
why: The removed inline handler wrote e.target.value, briefly making the sentinel the answer.
replace:
var sel = el("select", { id: "wiz-home_dashboard",
      onchange: function (e) { typed.home_dashboard = e.target.value; paintHomeDashboardChoice(); } });
asserts: theSentinelIsNeverPostedAsADashboardPath

name: no-dashboards-disables-the-control
why: That state is exactly when a path must be typed by hand; disabling it is a dead end.
asserts: customStaysReachableWhenTheAccountListsNoDashboards

name: empty-catalogue-disables-the-picker
why: Disabling the control when the account lists no dashboards is a dead end in the one state where a path must be typed by hand.
asserts: Custom is reachable when the account can see no dashboards at all

name: abandoned-custom-path-blocks-every-later-save
why: A hidden control left invalid refuses Save with nothing on screen to fix, because reportValidity() cannot surface an invisible field.
asserts: A malformed Custom path left behind never blocks a later Auto or listed save

name: account-default-spellings-stored-verbatim
why: A stored `/` or `/?kiosk` is absent from the dashboard list, so the renderer follows Auto while both pickers reopen in Custom.
asserts: every account-default spelling is stored as the blank sentinel

name: validity-delegated-to-the-browser-pattern-engine
why: An HTML pattern that will not compile under the v flag is ignored outright, so the check silently never runs.
asserts: neitherSurfaceDelegatesPathValidityToTheBrowsersPatternEngine

name: canonical-blank-discarded-as-a-no-op
why: Comparing renderer semantics makes canonicalization unreachable: choosing Auto over a stored `/` is skipped and the stale spelling reopens the picker in Custom.
asserts: choosing the account default over a legacy root spelling reaches storage

name: client-stricter-than-the-server
why: A client stricter than the authority blocks a legal route, worst when the catalogue is unavailable and Custom is the only way in.
asserts: The client never refuses a dashboard route the server would accept
